title: Devilled eggs
subtitle: Hard-boiled eggs filled with a seasoned yolk cream
excerpt: Devilled eggs are hard-boiled eggs halved and filled with a smooth paste of their own yolks mixed with mayonnaise, mustard, and a dash of hot sauce, then dusted with smoked paprika. They are a standard at American picnics, church potlucks, and Southern gatherings. Takes about 20 minutes.
sourceNotes: American culinary tradition. Devilled eggs appear in Fannie Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896), Project Gutenberg, as stuffed eggs. The mayonnaise-based version became standard in the mid-twentieth century.

recipe.yieldDescription: 24 devilled egg halves (serves 6 to 8 as a starter)
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 4 hours ahead and keep covered in the fridge.

content.text: Devilled eggs start with properly hard-boiled eggs that peel cleanly. The yolks are mashed with mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, a small amount of hot sauce, and a touch of vinegar to sharpen the whole thing. The mixture is spooned or piped back into the whites and dusted with smoked paprika.

Bring a pan of water to the boil. Lower the 12 eggs in gently and cook for exactly 11 minutes for fully set yolks without a green ring. Transfer to a bowl of cold water and leave for 5 minutes. Peel carefully.

Halve the eggs lengthways. Pop the yolks into a bowl. Add {{mayonnaise}} of mayonnaise, {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, {{louisiana-hot-sauce}} of hot sauce, {{cider-vinegar}} of cider vinegar, salt, and pepper. Mash until completely smooth.
Spoon or pipe the filling into the egg white halves. Dust with smoked paprika. Refrigerate until serving.

items.cause: Very fresh eggs; the membrane clings to the white.
items.fix: Use eggs that are at least 4 days old. Cooling quickly in cold water after cooking also helps.
11 minutes is the maximum. Transfer to cold water immediately.

content.text: Top with a small piece of crisp bacon, a slice of jalapeño, or a single prawn. For a sharper filling, replace half the mayonnaise with soured cream. A pinch of curry powder in the filling gives a more complex result.

Devilled eggs are the standard American picnic and potluck dish. They appear at every Southern outdoor gathering, church social, and holiday spread. Their simplicity and crowd appeal have made them one of the most widely made starters in the American home-cooking repertoire.
